_help.what: FAROUK's own stated trading rules, plus how check_rules.py assesses each one against the paper log. EDIT the 'statement' text freely (plain English). The 'check' field tells the tool HOW to look for the rule in the logged data.

checks_available.stop_present: Compliant if the filled trade has a stop-loss price logged; breaking if not.
checks_available.risk_pct_band: Compliant if risk per trade is within params.min_pct..max_pct (percent). params: {min_pct, max_pct}.
checks_available.notes_evidence: Looks for params.keywords in the trade notes. params.shows='compliance' (a hit = evidence the rule WAS followed; no hit = undetermined) or 'breach' (a hit = evidence it was BROKEN; no hit = undetermined).
checks_available.one_trade_per_day: Proxy for 'one good trade is enough': a trade on a single-trade day is compliant; a trade on a day with several entries is a possible breach.
checks_available.logs_misses_not_chase: Evidence the trader logs MISSED entries (and uses LIMIT-order sources) rather than chasing. Reported as evidence; chasing itself isn't directly loggable.
checks_available.not_detectable: The log cannot show this rule. params.reason explains why. Always reported as 'can't determine from data'.

_help.honesty: Where the data cannot show whether a rule was followed, the tool says 'can't determine from data' rather than guessing. Absence of evidence is NOT counted as a breach.

rules.statement: Small / consistent size only (risk 0.5-1% per trade)

params.reason: leverage isn't recorded in the paper log — only size/notional are, which is not the same thing

rules.statement: Move stop loss to entry (breakeven) once 50-100 pips in profit
Take partial profits as price moves
If you miss the entry, do not chase (use limit orders)
One good trade is enough — protect capital
Don't trade when emotional / during high-impact news
